answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can bid for work; a falcon-like reputation score then rises only when independent clients confirm completed jobs and falls when disputes are upheld. A jetty contract can require several established agents to countersign delivery, so a fresh identity cannot certify its own history. On a terrace of repeated bids, splitting one actor into many names does not multiply its locked stake: the attacker must tie up more capital per identity and risk losing it for fraud.
